transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-13 15:30 PST | Duration: 52m | Recording ID: ff-20261113-signet-9843
Attendees: Ava Moran (Redwood AE), Diego Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Signet Head of Search), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Marta Ruiz (Data Science), Samir Patel (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Signet evaluating where to run embedding generation and rerank: hosted Redwood API vs Dedicated reserved pools vs Private (VPC).
- Primary concerns: throughput (peak 8k qps, steady 80-200 qps), tail latency (<120ms for 95th on embed+rerank path), index size and sharding for vector DB, SSO/KMS and audit logs.
- Next step: bench plan for mixed fanout + rerank with ~100k queries/day; send pricing and SOC2 docs.

Topics covered:
- current stack and painpoints
- embedding dimensionality & quantization tradeoffs
- hybrid search + rerank architecture (vector DB + Redwood rerank/embed pipeline)
- hosting options: hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC
- security/compliance: SSO, KMS, audit logs
- pilot success criteria and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Moran: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll give like an overview then dig into the throughput bits, quick intros?
[00:08] Priya Kapoor: hi i'm Priya, lead search at Signet. main problem is recommendations + search relevance slipping during big campaigns. we have spikes, and our current vector db can't handle rerank fanout well.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Liam here, platform eng, we manage the cluster and infra, we've tried a few managed vdbs but costs balloon once we do rerank at scale.
[00:27] Marta Ruiz: Marta, data science, doing embedding models and metric tuning.
[00:31] Diego Chen: Diego from Redwood, i'll be the SE, i'll try to capture perf constraints and propose benchs. quick q: what are your target qps and p95 goals?
[00:40] Priya Kapoor: baseline - steady 80 qps, spikes to 8k qps for promos for about 10-20 mins; rerank path is embed->vdb topK(200)->rerank top10 with a 3-4k token prompt for context. p95 overall we'd like under 250ms, ideally <120ms for rerank-only flows? not sure is that realistic.
[01:02] Diego Chen: ok, so two things to split - embeddings fanout (search) and the rerank generation. are you generating embeddings in-line or pre-computing?
[01:11] Priya Kapoor: embeddings are pre-computed for catalog but on the user side we generate query embedding on request. the expensive part is the rerank call to an LLM after vector fanout.
[01:20] Ava Moran: to clarify, Redwood supports a few hosting paths: hosted API (fast onramp), Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and Private/VPC for network-isolated deployments. dedicated can give you pinned capacity for the rerank stage to hit tail+sla.
[01:36] Samir Patel: on the security side, we need SAML SSO, KMS integration for encryption at rest, and full audit logs — it's a req for the payments team.
[01:44] Diego Chen: Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC peering and KMS/HSM options; we also produce audit logs and retention policies. on perf: with dedicated capacity you can tune batching and kv-cache to get per-token cost down.
[01:58] Priya Kapoor: what's kv-cache? i've seen mentions of KV cache in your docs but not sure how that interacts with rerank?
[02:05] Diego Chen: kv-cache is the key-value cache for model kv states — for chat it's helpful, for single-turn rerank it's less useful, but prefix caching and request-level batching can save tokens. sometimes the doc says KV cash in notes, sorry for the typo, that's a transcription artifact.
[02:21] Liam O'Connor: walking through our infra: we run a multi-region k8s cluster, our vector DB is self-hosted (Milvus evaluation) but we're open to Redwood-managed hosting for embeddings generation if the economics work. index size right now ~18TB for dense vectors at 1536 dims, with 3 replicas for redundancy.
[02:40] Marta Ruiz: 1536 dims — we experimented with 768 and 384 for cheaper tails, but saw recall drop ~3-6% at 384. would a quantized embedding pipeline help?
[02:50] Diego Chen: yes, quantization (8-bit, product quant) can reduce storage and speed up nearest neighbor compute; Redwood Optimize gives recommendations for quant vs dims tradeoffs by workload. but quantization can impact downstream rerank recall — often you rerank using a small LLM to recover precision.
[03:06] Priya Kapoor: can we run 2-tier: cheap dense at 384 for initial fanout and then rerank with full-precision for top10? that would help costs.
[03:14] Ava Moran: that's a common hybrid: coarse embedding fanout then rerank. Redwood supports multi-model routing—route cheap embed to cheap index, then route topk to higher-fidelity rerank models or even host rerank on Dedicated capacity.
[03:26] Samir Patel: network egress between our VPC and a hosted API is a compliance red flag. we'd prefer a VPC peering or Private deployment. can Redwood Private live in our VPC?
[03:36] Diego Chen: yes, Redwood Private can be deployed with customer-managed VPC peering, and the control plane can be in your account in an apron model; we can also package on-prem for air-gapped. there are setup timelines and infra requirements.
[03:48] Liam O'Connor: timeline is tight — business wants a pilot during holiday season (dec window). what kind of ramp for Private vs Dedicated?
[03:56] Ava Moran: hosted: minutes to hours; Dedicated: 2-3 weeks provisioning for reserved pools; Private/VPC: typically 4-8 weeks depending on network and compliance checks. for a quick pilot we recommend hosted with strict IP allowlist or a temporary VPC tunnel.
[04:11] Priya Kapoor: pricing model — we need per-token for hosted, reserve commit for Dedicated. can you share an econ example for hybrid fanout?
[04:20] Ava Moran: yes we'll send a pricing spreadsheet. example: if you offload heavy rerank to Dedicated with a 2x reserved instance you get better per-token vs burst on hosted; we can model your 8k spike scenario.
[04:31] Marta Ruiz: micro-bench: what will you need from us to run the SE led test?
[04:36] Diego Chen: sample queries, index snapshot (anonymized), QPS schedule, and an infra endpoint for VDB if you want end-to-end. we can also run an A/B where we host embeddings on Redwood and signet keeps VDB to compare latency and cost.
[04:50] Priya Kapoor: on the index size — 18TB at 1536 dims, what's the recommended sharding strategy? we saw sharding issues with our current provider.
[04:59] Diego Chen: three options: single large cluster with sharding on the VDB side, hybrid fanout across regionally located indices, or use Redwood to serve embeddings and do top-k locally. If you keep the vector DB self-hosted, we recommend smaller shard sizes with consistent hashing so individual shard hotness doesn't cause tail spikes. we can share a sharding playbook.
[05:19] Liam O'Connor: what about tail latency on rerank — if we do top200 fanout then rerank top10, the network hop to VDB then LLM call causes variability. how do you ensure p95?
[05:29] Diego Chen: there are three levers: keep rerank on Dedicated pinned capacity to avoid cold starts, use async prefetching/cache for common queries, and route by policy — low-cost path for non-critical queries, high-precision path for paid customers. also set per-route latency SLOs in Redwood Console.
[05:45] Priya Kapoor: any reference for customers who did similar holiday ramp?
[05:48] Ava Moran: we have a retail customer case study (we'll share link) who used Dedicated + prefix cache to handle 10k burst with p95 ~180ms on rerank.
[05:57] Marta Ruiz: about model selection — do you host open models only or do you support fine-tuned models we bring?
[06:03] Diego Chen: we host both open model catalog and can accept new model tarballs; for private we can deploy your proprietary models in your VPC. model quantization is supported but for sensitive models we'd recommend Private.
[06:15] Samir Patel: security — SSO and audit logs, plus KMS. is the audit log accessible via SIEM integration?
[06:22] Ava Moran: yes, logs can stream to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) via secure forwarding; we also provide event-level audit logs for model calls and admin actions.
[06:32] Priya Kapoor: what about data retention/forget rules? we can't keep query logs for more than 30 days in raw form.
[06:38] Diego Chen: retention policies are configurable; you can opt-out of storing user inputs, or store aggregated metrics only. we'll provide compliance docs.
[06:46] Liam O'Connor: from infra POV, what's the CPU/GPU mix for Dedicated rerank pools? we want to know VM sizes and GPU types.
[06:54] Diego Chen: typical rerank LLMs run on A100 or H100 equivalents; for lower-cost options we use quantized LLM on T4/RTX-class; we'll include a matrix in the bench plan showing throughput per GPU, token/sec, and recommended batch sizes.
[07:09] Priya Kapoor: would you recommend quantizing the reranker too? worried about hallucinations.
[07:14] Diego Chen: quantized rerankers often maintain ranking fidelity for pairwise preferences, but you should run eval sets. we suggest a hybrid: full precision for a small critical cohort, quantized for background traffic. Redwood Optimize can suggest a quant/profile.
[07:28] Ava Moran: let's walk through a proposed pilot: 1) SE bench using 10k anchors, 100k queries/day synthetic schedule; 2) compare hosted vs dedicated for rerank latency & cost; 3) if VPC required, spin up Private PoC in isolated env for compliance checks.
[07:44] Priya Kapoor: that works. timeline — if bench week of 11/29, then decision by mid-December?
[07:51] Ava Moran: feasible. we'll try to turn pricing and docs around by Tuesday (11/16) so you can review.
[07:57] Marta Ruiz: a detail — when you say batch sizes, what are typical batch sizes for rerank to preserve low latency?
[08:02] Diego Chen: for rerank small LLMs, batch size 1-4 is common to keep tail low; for embeddings generation we can batch bigger (16-128) depending on latency tolerance.
[08:12] Samir Patel: can Redwood integrate with our internal key manager (Thales) for HSM?
[08:17] Ava Moran: yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations; exact model depends on Dedicated vs Private. Private gives you more control.
[08:25] Priya Kapoor: question about observability — we need token-level cost and latency by route, per-model.
[08:31] Diego Chen: Redwood Console provides per-route breakdowns and traces; we can export traces to your APM.
[08:38] Liam O'Connor: anything we should be worried about switching embedding dims from 1536 to 768? recall drop you mentioned — what numbers should we expect?
[08:46] Marta Ruiz: (interrupting) in our experiments switching to 768 decreased recall for tail categories by ~6% — that's non-trivial for long-tail SKUs.
[08:53] Diego Chen: often tradeoff is OK if reranker recovers rank for top items — reality is you need to run a small offline eval with your dataset. Diego will include recommended eval prompts in the bench plan.
[09:05] Priya Kapoor: any quick wins to reduce cost without sacrificing precision?
[09:09] Ava Moran: implement hybrid fanout with low-dim coarse vectors, rerank topN with high-fidelity model deployed on Dedicated for critical queries; add prefix caching for common queries; tune topK to minimize rerank load.
[09:24] Priya Kapoor: what's Redwood's SLA for Dedicated?
[09:27] Ava Moran: Dedicated has uptime SLA and latency targets we can discuss in an enterprise contract; we'll include the SLA summary.
[09:36] Liam O'Connor: can we do a short performance smoke test now? we have a tiny anonymized index that represents tail behavior.
[09:40] Diego Chen: yes we can schedule a short 1-2 hour smoke run as a pre-step before the bigger bench; need endpoints and small dataset.
[09:47] Priya Kapoor: ok we'll get that out.
[09:49] Ava Moran: to recap next steps — we'll send pricing, SOC2/SSO/KMS docs, Diego will produce bench plan and infra checklist, Signet will provide anonymized index and QPS targets.
[09:59] Priya Kapoor: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[10:02] Ava Moran: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench week.
